question.text: Who are eligible to participate in exchange-traded Interest Rate Futures in India?

answer.text: Any person resident in India, and non-residents such as FPIs to the extent specified, including banks, primary dealers, mutual funds, insurance companies and other entities subject to applicable regulator conditions
Only scheduled commercial banks and primary dealers
Only institutional investors such as banks and mutual funds

explanation.text: The Logic: The source states that any person resident in India and any non-resident to the extent specified are eligible to participate in Interest Rate Derivatives. FPIs are non-residents who may participate subject to specified limits, and regulated entities such as banks, primary dealers, mutual funds and insurance companies participate subject to their respective regulators' terms. The Trap: The framework is broader than only banks and primary dealers, and it is not restricted to institutional investors or only SEBI-registered entities. At the same time, FPIs are non-residents subject to specific limits, not residents in India, so eligibility cannot be described as residents-only. Note: Eligibility combines two streams under the source: persons resident in India, and non-residents (including FPIs) to the extent specified, with regulated entities also subject to conditions set by their own regulators.
